## Hands-on 4 – Exploring the menu {#hands-on-4-exploring-the-menu .smaller}

::: {.small}
**Task 4 is exploratory.** Try several specifications, look at what each one does, and get a feel for which decisions move the estimate.

1. Start from the reference: `try_spec()`
2. Change **one decision**, for example `try_spec(controls = "none")`, and read the estimate, its test and its place among the `r nrow(curve)`; `my_experiments()` lists every try
3. Do it again with a different decision. Three or four is plenty, and ask for one option that is off the curve, such as `try_spec(concern = "culture")`, to read why it is refused
4. Rerun the one that you can argue for best, so that it is your last try, and **submit it** with `submit_exploration()`
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Your result appears on the live **Multiverse** page within seconds, as an open circle.
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
This is **not** your preregistered analysis. You are allowed to look, change your mind and try again, which is why this phase has a name of its own.
:::

::: notes
This is where you get your hands properly dirty. Task 4 is exploration. Start from the reference with try underscore spec and no arguments, which gives point one seven five. Then change one decision and read what happens to the estimate, its test and its place among the hundred and ninety-two. Every try is logged, and my underscore experiments lists them side by side. Do it again with a different decision; three or four goes is plenty. Ask for one option that is off the curve as well, such as a single item for concern, and read the reason that comes back with the refusal. Then rerun the one you can argue for best and send it with submit underscore exploration. [advance] Your result appears on the Multiverse page within seconds. [advance] And this is not your preregistered analysis: here you may look, change your mind and try again.
:::
